_comment_sync: The quorum is declared once, here, and both the deployment and the assertions read this single declaration. num_sync is 2, not the role default of 1: with three standbys, ANY 2 keeps two remote durable copies and still tolerates one standby outage, which is the policy the production-readiness review recommends for a consistency-first design. Leaving synchronous_standby_names empty is deliberate -- it forces the role to build the value from the fields below, so the generator and its assertions are actually exercised.
_comment_ssl: TLS is off in this case. The collection has no ACME/certbot integration (finding TLS-01), and its only built-in certificate path generates a private self-signed CA inside the database through the EDB sslutils extension (TLS-03), which is not the ACME-issued chain the target deployment assumes. Turning pg_ssl on here would test sslutils, not the deployment. The TLS gap is asserted directly in test_prod_topology.py instead.
_comment_failover: repmgr_failover is left at the role default so the deployment test observes the shipped behaviour rather than a corrected one. test_prod_topology.py asserts what the default actually produces (finding EDB-01).
